questions.question: Which meta tag specifies the summary text displayed beneath a page title in Google search results?
questions.explanation: The meta description tag provides the concise snippet displayed in search engine result pages (SERPs).

questions.question: What does <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow"> instruct web crawlers to do?
options: Do not index this page in search results, and do not follow any links on it
Prioritize this page on mobile search
Delete the website from the web host
questions.hint: noindex prevents listing; nofollow prevents link crawling.
questions.explanation: 'noindex' blocks search engines from showing the page in search results; 'nofollow' stops crawlers from traversing its links.

questions.question: Which metadata standard uses og: prefixed properties for rich social media cards?
questions.explanation: The Open Graph protocol (created by Facebook) uses og: properties to control how URLs appear when shared on social networks.

questions.question: What is the purpose of <link rel="canonical" href="...">?
options: To tell search engines which URL is the master authoritative version, preventing duplicate content penalties
To automatically translate the page to English
questions.hint: Canonical indicates the primary official URL.
questions.explanation: The canonical link tag informs search engines of the primary authoritative URL when identical content exists across multiple URLs.

questions.question: Why should <meta charset="UTF-8"> be placed early in the <head> element?
options: So the browser knows how to decode incoming bytes before encountering non-ASCII characters
To make CSS files download faster
Because UTF-8 is required for JavaScript functions
questions.hint: The character encoding must be known before parsing text.
questions.explanation: Declaring charset early in <head> ensures the browser decodes all subsequent title and metadata characters with the correct Unicode mapping.
